title: Review and Reading Practice
objectives: Review all five noun declensions (focus on 1st, 2nd, 3rd)
Review all four verb conjugations in present tense
Read and translate connected Latin passages

grammar.explanation: This lesson reviews all major concepts from the beginner curriculum: noun declensions, verb conjugations, adjective agreement, and prepositions. Mastery of these fundamentals is essential for reading Latin texts.
rules: Nouns: learn nominative, genitive, and gender for each
Verbs: learn principal parts; infinitive shows conjugation
Adjectives: match gender, number, case with their noun
Word order is flexible; look for endings, not position

exercises.question: Translate: Milites fortes pro patria pugnant.
exercises.answer: Brave soldiers fight for the fatherland.

exercises.question: Translate: Rex bonus cives amat; cives regem laudant.
exercises.answer: The good king loves the citizens; the citizens praise the king.
hints: Note the case changes for rex/regem

exercises.question: Parse each word: Poeta fabulam longam narrat.
exercises.answer: Poeta (nom sg m), fabulam (acc sg f), longam (acc sg f), narrat (3rd sg pres)

exercises.prompt: Write 'The students always read good books in school' in Latin
exercises.sampleAnswer: Discipuli libros bonos in schola semper legunt.

culturalNote: Completing this beginner curriculum prepares you to read adapted Latin texts and begin encountering real Roman authors. The Romans left a vast literary heritage spanning history, philosophy, poetry, and rhetoric.

readingPassage.latin: Roma urbs magna et antiqua est. In Roma templa pulchra et viae longae sunt. Cives Romani in foro ambulant et de rebus publicis loquuntur. Senatores in Curia sedent et de legibus dicunt. Milites fortes pro patria pugnant. Poetae fabulas narrant; discipuli in scholis libros legunt. Lingua Latina per totum orbem terrarum nota est. Nunc nos quoque Latine discimus et loquimur.
readingPassage.translation: Rome is a great and ancient city. In Rome there are beautiful temples and long roads. Roman citizens walk in the forum and speak about public affairs. Senators sit in the Curia and speak about laws. Brave soldiers fight for the fatherland. Poets tell stories; students read books in schools. The Latin language is known throughout the whole world. Now we too learn and speak Latin.
notes: res publica: public affairs, the state
orbis terrarum: the circle of lands, the world
